questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State Ohm's law. *[2 marks]*

In an experiment to verify the relationship between the current, I, flowing through a conductor, and the potential difference, V, across its terminals, a student obtained the following data:

| V/V | 0.0 | 1.5 | 3.0 | 4.5 | 6.0 | 8.0 | 9.0 | 10.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I/A | 0.0 | 1.1 | 2.1 | 3.2 | 4.4 | 5.7 | 6.4 | 7.1 |

(ii) Plot a graph of potential difference, V, on the y-axis against current, I, on the x-axis. *[5 marks]*

(iii) Determine the gradient of the graph and state its significance. *[3 marks]*

(iv) What is the current in the circuit when the potential difference is 7.5 V? Show clearly how you arrived at your answer. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Ohm's law: the **current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends**, provided its temperature and other physical conditions remain constant ($V = IR$).

(ii) **Graph to plot (described).** Axes: I/A on the x-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{A}$, from 0 to 8) and V/V on the y-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{V}$, from 0 to 10), both labelled with units. Plot the eight points $(I, V)$: $(0, 0)$, $(1.1, 1.5)$, $(2.1, 3.0)$, $(3.2, 4.5)$, $(4.4, 6.0)$, $(5.7, 8.0)$, $(6.4, 9.0)$, $(7.1, 10.0)$. Draw the **best straight line through the origin** (a line from $(0, 0)$ to about $(7.1, 10.0)$, with the points scattered evenly on both sides of it).

(iii) Choose a large triangle on the line, for example between $(0, 0)$ and $(7.1, 10.0)$:

gradient $= \dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta I} = \dfrac{10.0 - 0}{7.1 - 0} = 1.4\,\Omega$ (a least-squares fit through all the points gives $1.40\,\Omega$).

**Significance:** the gradient of the V-I graph is the **resistance $R$ of the conductor** ($R = V/I$). It is constant, so the conductor obeys Ohm's law.

(iv) From the graph: draw a horizontal line from $V = 7.5\,\mathrm{V}$ on the y-axis to the line, then a vertical line down to the I axis and read the current there: $I \approx 5.4\,\mathrm{A}$.

Check by calculation: $I = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{7.5}{1.4} = 5.4\,\mathrm{A}$, so **$I \approx 5.4\,\mathrm{A}$** (accept a reading between $5.2$ and $5.5\,\mathrm{A}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A wire of a given length and thickness is connected to a circuit containing an ammeter and a battery.

(i) Define electromotive force. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Explain what will happen to the current flowing through the ammeter if the wire is replaced with a thinner wire of the same material and length. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a source is the **energy (work) converted by the source into electrical energy per unit charge** that passes through it, that is, the work done to drive one coulomb of charge round the complete circuit. $E = W/Q$; unit: volt (V).

(ii) The resistance of a wire is $R = \dfrac{\rho L}{A}$. A thinner wire has a **smaller cross-sectional area $A$**, so with the same material ($\rho$) and length ($L$) its **resistance is greater**. The battery gives the same voltage, so $I = V/R$ **decreases**: the ammeter reading falls.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State the function of a fuse and also state where it is connected in an electrical circuit. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Explain how the fuse performs the function stated in c (i) above. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A fuse is a **safety device that breaks the circuit when the current becomes too large**, so that the appliance and the wiring are protected from overheating and fire. It is connected **in series with the appliance, in the live wire** (before the appliance, between the supply and the appliance).

(ii) When an excessive current flows, the thin fuse wire (which has a low melting point) **heats up** because of the heating effect of the current ($P = I^2R$). When the current exceeds its rating, the wire **melts**, so the circuit is broken and the current stops.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State Snell's law of refraction. *[2 marks]*

In an experiment to verify Snell's law of refraction, a student put some water in a long glass jar and dropped a coin at the bottom. Then he measured the real depth and the apparent depth for different levels of water and obtained the following data.

| Real depth /cm | 0 | 5.0 | 8.0 | 10.0 | 12.0 | 15.0 | 18.0 | 20.0 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apparent depth / cm | 0.0 | 3.8 | 6.0 | 7.4 | 9.2 | 11.5 | 13.6 | 15.4 |

(ii) Plot a graph of real depth on the y-axis against apparent depth on the x-axis. *[5 marks]*

(iii) Determine the gradient of your graph and state its significance. *[3 marks]*

(iv) What will be the apparent position of the coin when the level of the water is $14.0\,\mathrm{cm}$? Show clearly how you arrived at your answer. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Snell's law: for a ray of light passing from one medium into another, the **ratio $\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r}$ is a constant** for the two media, where $i$ is the angle of incidence and $r$ the angle of refraction (this constant is the refractive index of the second medium relative to the first).

(ii) **Graph to plot (described).** Axes: apparent depth/cm on the x-axis (scale $1\,\mathrm{cm}$ to $1\,\mathrm{cm}$, from 0 to 16) and real depth/cm on the y-axis (from 0 to 20), both labelled with units. Plot the eight points (apparent, real): $(0, 0)$, $(3.8, 5.0)$, $(6.0, 8.0)$, $(7.4, 10.0)$, $(9.2, 12.0)$, $(11.5, 15.0)$, $(13.6, 18.0)$, $(15.4, 20.0)$. Draw the **best straight line through the origin**.

(iii) Take a large triangle, for example from $(0, 0)$ to $(15.4, 20.0)$:

gradient $= \dfrac{\Delta(\text{real depth})}{\Delta(\text{apparent depth})} = \dfrac{20.0}{15.4} \approx 1.3$ (a least-squares fit through all the points gives $1.31$).

**Significance:** the gradient equals $\dfrac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}}$, which is the **refractive index $n$ of water** ($n \approx 1.3$). A straight line through the origin shows that the ratio is constant, as Snell's law requires.

(iv) From the graph: draw a horizontal line from a real depth of $14.0\,\mathrm{cm}$ on the y-axis to the line, then a vertical line down to the x-axis and read the apparent depth: about $10.7\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Check by calculation: apparent depth $= \dfrac{\text{real depth}}{n} = \dfrac{14.0}{1.31} \approx 10.7\,\mathrm{cm}$.

**The coin appears to be about $10.7\,\mathrm{cm}$ below the water surface** (accept $10.5$ to $10.8\,\mathrm{cm}$).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Define total internal reflection. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State the two conditions necessary for total internal reflection to occur. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Total internal reflection is the **complete reflection of light back into the denser medium at the boundary with a less dense medium**, when the angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle (no light is refracted out).

(ii) (1) The light must travel **from a denser medium to a less dense medium** (for example glass or water to air). (2) The **angle of incidence in the denser medium must be greater than the critical angle** for the two media.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Name one member of the electromagnetic spectrum and give its wavelength range. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Explain the use of the named member in f(i) and relate it to its property. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **X-rays**, with a wavelength range of about $10^{-11}\,\mathrm{m}$ to $10^{-8}\,\mathrm{m}$.

(ii) X-rays are used in **medical imaging to see broken bones** (and in security scanners). This relates to their property of having a **very short wavelength (high frequency, high energy)**: they penetrate soft tissue easily but are absorbed by dense bone, and they blacken photographic film, so a shadow picture of the bones is formed.

(Other acceptable answers: *microwaves*, wavelength about $1\,\mathrm{mm}$ to $30\,\mathrm{cm}$, used to cook food because water molecules absorb them and heat up; *infrared*, about $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m}$ to $10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m}$, used in remote controls and grills because hot bodies emit it and it is felt as heat; *ultraviolet*, about $10^{-8}\,\mathrm{m}$ to $4\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m}$, used to detect forged banknotes because some materials fluoresce.)
